# Research — Resume Approved Acceptance Fixture

This is synthetic acceptance data, not real market or customer research.

## Supported observations

- `CLM-001`: In the fictional Q2 cohort, 68 of 100 checklist-onboarding accounts and 60 of 100 standard-onboarding accounts were retained at day 90 (`SRC-001`, `SRC-003`). This is an observed 8 percentage-point difference, not a causal estimate.
- `CLM-002`: Median time to first value was six days in the checklist cohort and nine days in standard onboarding (`SRC-001`, `SRC-003`). Cohort assignment was not randomized.
- `CLM-003`: Four of six fictional interview participants said the checklist reduced setup ambiguity, while two still preferred a live kickoff for multi-team rollouts (`SRC-002`).

## Conflicts and limitations

The cohort data favors a checklist pilot, but interview evidence warns against replacing facilitated support for complex accounts. The cohort is fictional, non-randomized, from one product and one period, with no confidence interval or adjustment for account mix. The interview sample is small and self-selected. No claim establishes causality or generalizes beyond the fixture.

## Decision implication

The evidence supports a bounded pilot with predeclared success measures, not a universal self-service rollout. Preserve a facilitated path for complex accounts and measure cohort comparability.
